Definition: File formats: Use community accepted modern file formats such as CRAM.
DOIs: Pipelines should have digital object identifiers (DOIs).
Workflow size: Not too big, not too small.
Samplesheets should identify all files required as inputs for workflows. Avoid passing directories.
Variable names should only be used once and should be descriptive.
Any parameters you specify in a nextflow.config files should be defined in the schema.
Ensure all local, ph-core, and nf-core modules in the pipeline are being used.
All debug code should be removed
Reused code should be made into a function where possible
Confirm all links in documentation are correct and valid.
When declaring a variable, use def for consistency. (Note: scoping issues using nextflow version 24 might occur when using def in some scopes)_SUB
Avoid complex nested logic_SUB
If a file is being parsed multiple times streamline code where possible
Subworkflow must contain at least two modules
Subworkflow should utilze native nextflow toolings where possible
Remove .first() operator for channels with a single value
Variable names should only be used once and should be descriptive._SUB
All debug code should be removed_SUB
Reused code should be made into a function where possible_SUB
Each input and output channel SHOULD have a comment describing the output structure of the channel
Each input and output channel structure should also be described in the meta.yml in the description entry.
Tags for any dependent modules must be specified to ensure changes to upstream modules will re-trigger tests for the current subworkflow
The assertAll() function must be used to specify an assertion, and there must be a minimum of one success assertion and versions in the snapshot_SUB
All output channels should be present in the nf-test snapshot file, or at a minimum, it must be verified that the files exist.
There should be a test and assertions for each type of input and output_SUB
Test names should describe the test dataset and configuration used._SUB
Input channel declarations must be defined for all possible input files that will be required by the subworkflow (i.e. both required and optional files) within the take block.

Named file extensions should generally be emitted for all output channels(e.g. path "*.txt", emit:txt), but there can be exceptions, such as when the output is a dataset/directory(e.g., $prefix:directory from nextclade_datasetget)_SUB
Optional inputs are not currently supported by Nextflow. However, passing an empty list ([]) instead of a file as a subworkflow parameter can be used to work around this issue
Directory structure for the subworkflow name must be all lowercase
All parameter names must follow the snake_case convention
All function names must follow the camelCase convention
Channel names must follow snake_case convention and be all lower case
Input channel names should signify the input object type.
Output channel names SHOULD only be named based on the major output file of that channel (i.e, an output channel of [[meta], bam] should be emitted as bam, not ch_bam)
Named params defined in the parent workflow must not be assumed to be passed to the subworkflow to allow developers to call their parameters whatever they want.
Do not declare error strategies in a separate modules config file
All mandatory input files included in input channel definitions
All optional input files included in input channel definitions
Non-mandatory command line tool non-file arguments must be provided as a string via the $task.ext.args variable
Each command must have an $args variable. $args variables (e.g. $args, $args2, $args3) must correspong to order of tools presented in the command line
The process definition must not change the when statement
If needed,  use the shell "tee" command to capturing STDOUT and STDERR.
Stub block must exist for all modules
Module definitions with process blocks must be in order and no repeated “script:” blocks
Non-file mandatory commands should be a value channel
Limit multi-command piping unless there is a run-time, storage advantage in piping implementation
Inputs and outputs should be compressed, where applicable

If a tool does not exit with the expected exit code 0 upon successful use of the tool, use the || operator to run another useful command when the exit code is not 0 (for example, testing if a file is not size 0).
All code must be aligned to follow the ‘Harshil Alignment’ format

The recommended procedure is, once the alternative is available on nf-core modules, add a message to the top of the module code saying this module is deprecated, and an assert in the code body to print a deprecation message
Use only one tool per module if posible
If there is a conda declaration, ensure it is adheres to nf-core standards
Each module must have a meta.yaml in the same directory as the main.nf of the module itself
Tools section must list every tool used in the module
Tools section must have a args_id: field for every tool in the module that describes which $args ($args2, $args3) variable is used for that specific module.
Input and output tuples must be split into separate entries
Input/output types must only be of the following categories: map, file, directory, string, boolean, integer, float, boolean, list
Input/output entries MUST match a corresponding channel in the module itself
Input/output patterns (if present) must follow a Java glob pattern
Keywords should be sufficient to make the module findable through research domain, data types, and tool function keywords
Input and output sections of the meta.yaml should only have entries of input and output channels
Input/output descriptions should be descriptive of the contents of file
Confirm version is documented correctly in the versions.yml file. There should not be a v in front of the version number.
Input entries should be marked as Mandatory or Optional
A stub test must exist for the module
Tags for any dependent modules must be specified to ensure changes to upstream modules will re-trigger tests for the current module.
The assertAll() function must be used to specify an assertion, and there must be a minimum of one success assertion and versions in the snapshot
Only one snapshot is allowed per module test, which should contain all assertions present in this test.
There should be a test and assertions for each type of input and output
Test names should describe the test dataset and configuration used.
Input data should be referenced with the modules_testdata_base_path parameter
Preferentially use params.publish.dir mode instead of hard coded copy setting
Input channel path declarations must be defined for all possible input files (i.e. both required and optional files)
Options, flags, parameters that are not required by the tool to function should not be included as a val channel input- rather these can be passed via ext.args

Named file extensions should generally be emitted for all output channels(e.g. path "*.txt", emit:txt), but there can be exceptions, such as when the output is a dataset/directory(e.g., $prefix:directory from nextclade_datasetget)
Generic auxiliary files used across different input files (e.g. common reference sequences) may be defined using a dedicated input channel (e.g. reference files)
Input channel val declarations should be defined for all mandatory non-file inputs that are essential for the functioning of the tool (e.g. parameters, flags etc)
Optional inputs are not currently supported by Nextflow. However, passing an empty list ([]) instead of a file as a module parameter can be used to work around this issue
Optional outputs should be marked as optional
Each output file type should be emitted in its own channel (and no more than one), along with the meta map if provided ( the exception is the versions.yml).
Directory structure for the module name must be all lowercase, and without punctuation, e.g. modules/nf-core/bwa/mem/. The name of the software (i.e. bwa) and tool (i.e. mem) MUST be all one word
Process name in the module file must be all uppercase e.g. process BWA_MEM {. The name of the software (i.e. BWA) and tool (i.e. MEM) MUST be all one word separated by an underscore
Parameter names must follow the snake_case convention
Function names must follow the camelCase convention
Channel names must follow snake_case convention and be all lower case

Output file (and/or directory) names should generally consist of only ${prefix} and the file-format_suffix(e.g., ${prefix}.fq.gz), but there can be exceptions, such as when the output is a dataset/directory(e.g., $prefix:directory from nextclade_datasetget)
All params within the module must only be initialised and used in the local context of the module.
Any parameters that need to be evaluated in the context of a particular sample e.g. single-end/paired-end data must also be defined within the process
A module file should only define input and output files as command-line parameters to be executed within the process
An appropriate resource label must be provided for the module as listed in the nf-core pipeline template e.g. process_single, process_low, process_medium or process_high
If the tool supports multi-threading then you must provide the appropriate parameter using the Nextflow task variable e.g. --threads $task.cpus
If the tool does not support multi-threading, consider process_single unless large amounts of RAM are required
If a module contains multiple tools that supports multi-threading (e.g. piping output into a samtools command), you can assign CPUs per tool
Software requirements should be declared within the module file using the Nextflow container directive
If required, multi-tool containers may also be available on BioContainers e.g. bwa and samtools.
It is also possible for a new multi-tool container to be built and added to BioContainers by submitting a pull request on their multi-package-containers repository.
The new test data file within a branch (modules or pipelines) should not replicate existing test-data unless absolutely necessary
Test data must be publicly available and have licenses to allow public reuse
Test data should be as small as possible
Test data files SHOULD be described on the given branch’s README file, describing source, how generated, licenses etc.
When it is applicable, pre-existing files from nf-core/test-datasets will be reused if at all possible.
Test data files must have an entry in the nf-core/test-datasets repo README

It may not be possible to add test data for some modules e.g. if the input data is too large or requires a local database. In these scenarios, it is recommended to use the Nextflow stub feature to test the module.
Files should be generally organised based on existing structure, typically (for bioinformatics pipelines) by discipline, organism, platform or format
Downstream or related test-data files should be named based on the upstream file name

Implement the filtering logic if proper test samples are available, ensuring that the workflow can fail gracefully in the event of errors or invalid inputs (e.g., Adding warning messages when encountering insufficient data)
